title: Agreement with the empty-oracle simulation
statement: Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $c$ be a configuration. Suppose that at every time $s<t$, the run from $c$ by the plain machine simulating $M$ with the empty oracle is not in the query state. Then the configuration reached after $t$ steps by running $M$ with oracle $O$ from $c$ equals the configuration reached after $t$ steps by that plain machine.
hypotheses_covered: For every s<t, the plain empty-oracle run is not in the query state
